role_evidence.claim: Berkshire Hathaway is named as a partner alongside Chubb in the US International Development Finance Corporation maritime reinsurance facility created for Gulf marine war risk.
role_evidence.source_name: Insurance Business, Strait of Hormuz crisis: Why the biggest opportunity in marine war insurance lies ahead

role_evidence.claim: Berkshire Hathaway is ranked by AM Best as the second largest reinsurance group among non-IFRS-17 reporters.
role_evidence.source_name: Insurance Journal, Munich Re, Lloyd's Top List of 50 Largest Global Reinsurers: AM Best
role_evidence.source_excerpt: Lloyd's (in the non-IFRS-17 group of reinsurers) is followed by Berkshire Hathaway at number two, Reinsurance Group of America Inc. (RGA) in third place and Everest Re coming in at number four.

business_summary: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. (NYSE: BRK.B) is a diversified US holding company whose insurance and reinsurance operations sit alongside railroad, utility, manufacturing and retail businesses. It sits on the hormuz-maritime chain's war-risk-reinsurance-capacity and marine-war-risk-underwriting links. On war-risk-reinsurance-capacity: named partner insurer in the US International Development Finance Corporation maritime war-risk reinsurance facility, and the second largest non-IFRS-17 reinsurance group by AM Best's ranking. On marine-war-risk-underwriting: US ocean-marine underwriting group whose hull and cargo book reprices on the Gulf war-risk shock; ranked in the NAIC national ocean marine top ten.

exposure_summary.narrative: Berkshire Hathaway sits on two links: war-risk-reinsurance-capacity, scored EMERGING (impact 78, crowdedness 55, capture 52): capacity had to be manufactured rather than bought (a sovereign DFC facility and a separate Lloyd's market consortium), and the trade press's own read is that the episode has not been profitable in aggregate so far; and marine-war-risk-underwriting, scored CROWDED (impact 85, crowdedness 62, capture 45): the chain's own repricing_check reads ATTENTION_WITHOUT_EARNINGS (1 of 4 legs met) because no cited source sizes marine war revenue at any listed insurer even though the premium headline (war-risk cover from roughly 1-3% to 7.5-10% of hull value) has moved. On war-risk-reinsurance-capacity: Named partner insurer in the US International Development Finance Corporation maritime war-risk reinsurance facility, and the second largest non-IFRS-17 reinsurance group by AM Best's ranking. On marine-war-risk-underwriting: US ocean-marine underwriting group whose hull and cargo book reprices on the Gulf war-risk shock; ranked in the NAIC national ocean marine top ten.
